subject: Privstack: terraform proxy + eBPF network validation
messages:
From: Jordan Price <jordan.price@acmesys.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: acme-systems-networking@acmesys.com
Date: 2026-06-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: terraform plan + eBPF policy validation for private deployment

Hi Neha / Marissa,

Thanks again — our ops team at Acme is finalizing the private deployment terraform plan for the VPC+on-prem connector. There are two items we want Redwood to validate before we flip the CI gate:

- The terraform changes add an HA proxy layer (haproxy) in front of the model serving nodes; we need confirmation the subnet routing / route tables and NAT behavior won't break kv-cache replication.
- We're introducing an eBPF-based ingress policy (sample attached) to enforce service-level L7 filtering for East-West traffic inside the cluster. We want Redwood to confirm the policy and any kernel-level constraints for the supported host images.

Attached: terraform-plan-privstack-proxy.diff.txt, ebpf-policy-sample.yaml

Proposed validation window: June 2, 09:00-12:00 PT — we can provide a sandbox VPC and temporary creds.

Can you confirm what artifacts you need (plan, helm values, ansible playbook snippets)? Also let us know whether you need an on-site engineer for the kernel/eBPF checks.

Thanks,
Jordan Price
Principal Network Engineer — Acme Systems

- For eBPF, send the kernel version matrix of the host images — some older kernels need BTF or different compile flags.

I'll loop in Rishi (infra runtime) and Dylan (networking) to capture infra-level checks. If you'd like, Marissa can coordinate documentation and the runbook artifacts we produce.

I'll schedule a 2-hour slot and share a short checklist prior to the run.

Best,

Team — forwarding Acme's artifacts. TL;DR: they want us to validate terraform changes that place an HA proxy in a dedicated subnet, and an eBPF L7 ingress filter on hosts. Testing window is Jun 2 09:00-11:00 PT; sandbox env and firewall exceptions will be ready.

Please see inline asks below (I've pasted the original note at the bottom). I want a brief findings doc after the window covering: routing & NAT implications, helm/sa/hostNetwork risks, eBPF kernel compatibility, and CI gating changes.

Ask list:
- Rishi: run the terraform plan static scan and confirm public/private route table updates. Look for any cross-subnet references that could break KV cache traffic (redis/gossip). Provide a one-paragraph remediation for anything risky.

- Marissa: prepare a templated runbook (short) and evidence checklist we can hand back to Acme after the run.

Notes / constraints:
- Do not make changes to their terraform registry modules; treat this as validation only.
- If we find a kernel mismatch, propose a fallback: move to a userspace sidecar L7 filter (envoy) for those hosts as a temporary measure.

On Jun 2 I will be the primary contact and will consolidate notes.

Thanks — Neha

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: terraform plan + eBPF policy validation for private deployment

Quick summary from today's run (window: 09:00-11:00 PT):

Findings (high-level):
1) Terraform plan audit: the plan keeps control-plane endpoints and redis/gossip services in separate subnets but references a shared NAT gateway for outbound egress from the proxy subnet. This is acceptable for short-term but we recommend creating a dedicated NAT per AZ to avoid SNAT port exhaustion under heavy token-traffic. See remediation snippet: add aws_nat_gateway per az + route table splits.

2) KV cache implications: there were two incorrectly scoped security group rules allowing 0.0.0.0/0 for inbound between proxies and nodes in the plan; we flagged these with an example variable change. Recommend tightening to the proxy-subnet CIDR and adding an explicit ingress rule for the redis port range.

3) Helm/hostNetwork: the helm values include hostNetwork: true for the haproxy daemonset in one chart. That bypasses CNI-level filtering; eBPF policies applied at host-level will still see traffic but service affinity could change. Recommend running a canary with hostPort-only mapping instead of full hostNetwork to limit surface area.

4) eBPF/kernel: Dylan confirmed that host-image-5.4.0-42 lacks full BTF support required by the eBPF loader they proposed. Two options: upgrade kernel image to 5.10+ or compile a minimal eBPF program without BTF (we prefer kernel upgrade). For hosts that cannot upgrade immediately, suggest falling back to an Envoy sidecar for L7 filtering.

Action items produced:
- Rishi: submit a terraform variable patch to scope SGs and add nat-per-az — patch attached (terraform-plan-privstack-proxy.diff.txt).
- Dylan: produce a short eBPF compatibility matrix + recommended compile flags (attached: ebpf-policy-sample.yaml annotated).
- Marissa: runbook draft ready at https://redwood-internal.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-1254 — will send to Acme.

Closing note: no blocking issues found for go/no-go; most items are configuration hardening and kernel image alignment. Acme should prioritize kernel upgrades on any hosts they expect to enforce eBPF policies in production.

-rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Infra Runtime Lead, Redwood Inference
